newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU diplomat says agreement near on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: EU diplomat says agreement near on stability pact.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday were close to an agreement on a post-single currency stability pact, and had agreed most of the issues dividing them, an EU diplomat said.
"They are in the box," the diplomat told Reuters as negotiations moved into the evening.

The diplomat said that on the main issue dividing the ministers -- a definition of exceptional and temporary economic conditions under which a deficit would be allowed to rise above three percent of total output without penalty -- EU member states appeared to be heading towards a middle ground.
"Countries are now prepared to (accept) some sort of a figure for what is an exceptional circumstance," the diplomat said.

Going into the meeting, Germany had been demanding that the definition of an unusually severe recession be set at a contraction of two percent of GDP, while the European commission, backed by a number of other countries, had not wanted any figure to be specified.
The diplomat also said that the EU finance ministers had already agreed to a fixed level of fines.
Under the terms of the agreement, a country that allowed its deficit to exceed the three percent limit compared to GDP would be fined an initial 0.2 percent of GDP.
For each subsequent percentage point over the limit, a country would face a fine of 0.1 percent of GDP, running to a and a maximum ceiling of 0.5 percent, the diplomat said.
